title: The Gingerbread Man
author: Traditional
source: Public domain. Retold from the traditional tale, with a gentler ending.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time, a little old woman baked a gingerbread man. She gave him raisin eyes, a sugary smile, and three fine buttons of icing. But the moment she opened the oven — up he jumped, and out the door he ran!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the gingerbread man only laughed and called back over his shoulder,

segments.speaker: gingerbread
segments.text: "Run, run, as fast as you can! You can't catch me — I'm the Gingerbread Man!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He ran past the old man in the garden, past the cow in the meadow, and past the horse by the fence. They all chased after him — thump, clop, gallop! — but the gingerbread man was faster than them all.

segments.speaker: gingerbread
segments.text: "I've run from an old woman, an old man, a cow, and a horse! Run, run, as fast as you can — you can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At last he came to a wide river, and there he had to stop, for gingerbread men cannot swim. Along came a fox with a long red tail and a very polite smile.

segments.speaker: fox
segments.text: "Good day, little gingerbread man. What a fine runner you are! Might I carry you across the river on my tail?"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The gingerbread man looked behind him — the old woman, the old man, the cow, and the horse were getting closer! So he hopped onto the fox's tail, and the fox slipped into the water.

segments.speaker: fox
segments.text: "Dear me, the water is getting deep. Climb up on my back, little friend, so you don't get soggy."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The gingerbread man climbed onto the fox's back.

segments.speaker: fox
segments.text: "Deeper still! Quick — hop onto my nose, where it's nice and dry!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the gingerbread man hopped right onto the fox's nose. But just as the fox opened his mouth for a snap — SPLASH! A big river wave washed over them both, and the slippery wet gingerbread man slid clean off and was flung to the far bank.

segments.speaker: gingerbread
segments.text: "Too slow, Mister Fox! Run, run, as fast as you can!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The soggy fox sneezed and slunk away with an empty belly. And the gingerbread man? He ran all the way home to the little old woman — for even a gingerbread man gets tired of running — and he decided her cozy kitchen windowsill was the finest place in the world. She kept him there in a place of honor, sweet smile and all, and told this story to every child who visited. Snip, snap, that's that!
